title: Herod the Great rules Judea
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Taking the World for Jesus). Jones, Appendix F (23rd ed., 2026), sets the sort. The Generations dates below stay on display.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones): 37 BC (no higher-tier year available).

chronologies.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

chronologies.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 280 (PDF p. 315)
chronologies.note: This record is dated from Herod's taking of Jerusalem. Jones also prints "Rome appoints Herod the Great king" in 40 BC. That appointment is a separate line and is not used here.

chronologies.citation: Taking the World for Jesus, ch. 1 "The Roman Empire and the Men Who Turned the World Upside Down", PDF p. 16 (printed pp. 31–32)
chronologies.note: Ruled until shortly after Jesus was born.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 6 "The Special People of God", PDF p. 172 (printed p. 171)
chronologies.note: p. 510: Herod captures Jerusalem "By 37 BC" (Timeline Review p. 524: "Herod Captures Jerusalem 37 bc").
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "37–4 BC" (PDF p. 303): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 13 "The Special People of God–Taking the Promised Land", PDF p. 303 (printed p. 289)
Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 19 (PDF p. 28)
